 LISA Is a Boss In New PlayStation Spot Featuring ‘Tarantino’: Watch
 The BLACKPINK star gets her game on with PlayStation, for a promo that unlocks an extended preview of "Tarantino."
 By
 Lars Brandle

 Jeremy Chan/Getty Images 
 Trending on Billboard 
 LISA gets her game on with PlayStation , for a new spot that unlocks an extended preview of “Tarantino.”
 In the 50 second clip, the BLACKPINK  star enters a lift and goes straight to floor 5 — LISA’s penthouse. Before she reaches her destination, the K-pop star chooses a different quest as she grabs a limited-edition DualSense wireless controller and enters the worlds that are in the building, from Marvel Wolverine to Kena: Scars of Kosmora, God of War: Laufey, and Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.
 The soundbed is a preview of “Tarantino,” a track from her upcoming EP Press Play , due out Friday, Oct. 23.

 “Got my nails really long like the barrel of my gun and my lipstick all over your face,” she sings, over the top of a rolling beat. “I’m a boss, I’m a don when I’m driving to the sun. It’s a movie, baby, come and press play.”
 The campaign is an extension to the Thai rapper and singer’s global PS5 tie-in which kicked off last year, and includes the all-new DualSense hardware, which arrives Oct. 30 in limited quantities, is available for preorder at PlayStation and was designed with LISA’s help. 
 As previously reported, the partnership will splash out with official merchandise — including apparel, tote bags, hats, and more — available at LISA’s official Amazon store and PlayStation’s online store .
 LISA’s just getting started. A documentary about her first solo year apart from BLACKPINK, titled Always Lalisa , arrived in cinemas early this month, ahead of a Las Vegas residency due to get underway Nov. 12 at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace.
 LISA’s Press Play EP features the lead single “SaWaDiKa,”  which debuted at No. 69 on the Billboard Hot 100 and at No. 23 on the Billboard Global 200 in September. LISA dropped her debut solo album, Alter Ego , in 2025, peaking at No. 7 on the all-genres Billboard 200 .
